label: Sizes
description: Footprint seen from above, which sets the hitbox. Pick the band whose examples name what the unit is. Examples win over measurements, because strategy games draw soldiers oversized. A weight word in the unit's type (light, medium or heavy tank or mech) is not a size. Count the hull, fuselage and wings, not a rotor disc or a gun barrel. Only for a unit that no example covers, measure. Compare it with the same game's foot soldier: one soldier is small, two to three soldier-widths is medium. When it is wider than that, or the game has no foot soldiers, compare it with the game's main battle tank: clearly smaller is medium, about the same is large, twice or more is huge.

terms.label: Tiny
terms.description: Clearly smaller than one soldier of its own game: hand-sized or knee-high drones and bots, animals smaller than a dog. Hard to hit, easy to lose sight of. A unit the game handles like a soldier (it fills an infantry seat in a transport, or the game counts it as infantry) is small, however small it looks.

terms.label: Small
terms.description: One soldier: infantry, power-suit troopers, war dogs, and robots or drones the game handles like a soldier.

terms.label: Medium
terms.description: About two to three soldier-widths: buggies, cars, armoured cars, APCs and IFVs, light mechs and light walkers, light scout helicopters.

terms.label: Large
terms.description: Tanks of every weight (light, medium and heavy tanks, tank destroyers, self-propelled guns), carriers built on a tank hull, medium to assault mechs, attack and transport helicopters, jets.

terms.label: Huge
terms.description: Two tanks or more: super-heavies, giant mechs, airships.
